mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate environment consistently reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific trigger conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% (using 20-day rolling window), or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPI reading exceeding 215.0 indicates accelerating inflation, prompting the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, which typically causes a short-term decline in equity valuations over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 215.0, or the correlation between CPIAUCSL > 215.0 and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential sales (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) signal a weakening housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in RSAFS and HOUST fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 45% of cases over a 3-year rolling window, or the interaction term in a regression has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 7.5%), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when UNRATE > 7.5%, or the average return in high unemployment periods is not significantly higher than the overall average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity, which correlates with stronger corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days without requiring specific trigger conditions.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO is rising, or the Rank IC for INDPRO is below 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly housing starts figure below 450.0 thousand units signals a contraction in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of economic weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when HOUST < 450.0, or the correlation between HOUST < 450.0 and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in payroll employment (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicate a deteriorating labor market, which typically precedes a recession and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint decline in PAYEMS and rise in UNRATE fails to predict negative SPX returns in more than 45% of cases over a 3-year rolling window, or the interaction term in a regression has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes (GDPC1 > 11500.0 billion), the economy is strong and corporate earnings are robust, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 > 11500.0, or the average return in late-cycle periods is not significantly higher than the overall average (t-test p > 0.05).
